manage.lead: Monitor typical lesions in young children; excise in teens and adults.

points: Dermatology via the suspected cancer pathway; excision for histology.

items.t: Spitz-like lesion in an adolescent or adult; any atypical features.

quiz.q: Typical patient with a Spitz naevus?
quiz.a: A child with a fast-growing pink dome.
A pigmented spindle-cell naevus: dark symmetrical starburst, often on a young woman's thigh.
